result.title: DreamX: Video Diffusion Model is a Universal Latent Action Learner
result.summary: Learning a universal action representation from video requires modeling dynamics that are consistent across different executions of the same action yet invariant to changes in embodiment and appearance. Existing latent action models infer actions from visual transitions, but their representations often entangle the underlying action with irrelevant visual variations, limiting transfer across embodiments. We introduce DreamX, which repurposes a pretrained video diffusion model as a universal latent action learner. Our approach extracts compact latent actions from the video model's rich spatiotemporal features, compressing each latent video frame by $\boldsymbol{300\times}$ ($\boldsymbol{1{,}200 \rightarrow 4}$ tokens). In addition, by leveraging the video model's generative prior, these latent actions capture action-relevant dynamics disentangled from visual appearance. The resulting latent space serves as a shared action interface across embodiments (human and robot), environments, and action parameterizations. On LARY-Bench, DreamX achieves state-of-the-art performance among latent action models. Moreover, actions encoded in one setting remain effective in another: the latent space supports any-to-any video transfer and zero-shot action transfer across diverse embodiments and environments. Furthermore, this shared interface also enables policy learning in a compact latent action space, reducing the computational cost of video-diffusion-based policies.

AI.brief_summary: 将预训练视频扩散模型改造为通用 latent action 学习器，从其时空特征中提取紧凑 latent action，把每帧约 1200 个 token 压缩到 4 个，从而在跨具身、跨环境与不同动作参数化之间形成共享接口，用于视频迁移与紧凑空间中的策略学习。
AI.relevance_reason: 论文主题是动作表示与策略而非 VLM 推理，但其「用视频扩散先验把与动作相关的动态从外观中剥离并压至极少 token」的做法，可供核查 LVR 中视觉状态的高倍压缩与内容-外观分离是否会丢失任务必要细节。
